name: Parallel CPU ML training — Illustrative resource estimates, not measured production data
description: CPU-based dataset generation followed by concurrent SVM and Random Forest training, adapted from SeBS-Flow.
assumptions: Every edge is invoked once per successful workflow execution; N=100 is a synthetic profiling window.
CPU values are illustrative average active core equivalents; memory is illustrative peak host MiB per invocation, including runtime overhead. Neither was measured.
Local storage and external network values are bytes per function invocation. Edge request/response values are body-size budgets per call; they are excluded from node external-network totals.
External object stores, caches, and databases are not mergeable function nodes. Merging does not automatically remove their traffic.
Connection setup, retries, transport overhead, client-to-entry traffic, and execution timing are not modeled. No bandwidth rate or latency prediction is implied.
Zero means no modeled demand for this selected workload, not an observed production measurement.
The source uses orchestration/data dependencies. Here generate_dataset uploads the dataset, directly invokes both trainers asynchronously, and waits for completion.
Both trainers read the same object; their function calls carry references, not feature matrices. There is no local scratch file.
Float64 features, int64 labels, model artifact sizes, CPU/memory demand, and reference-envelope sizes are illustrative choices, not values reported by SeBS-Flow.
merging_questions: Is combining the generator with one or both trainers worthwhile when dataset transfer remains external?
Would concurrent CPU/memory demand outweigh eliminating two small reference-bearing calls?
Could an application rewrite pass the dataset directly, and how would that differ from merging alone?

attributes.role: Generate 500 x 1024 features and labels; upload one shared dataset
Read the dataset and train a CPU SVM; upload model
Read the same dataset and train a CPU Random Forest; upload model
